correctness.rationale: Independently recomputed every essential number with fresh code (no reuse of verify.py paths). mc7: 147 lines, all Latin 7x7, 0/147 CSV mismatches; headline (rowHam=1, colHam=2, symHam=1, atomic=1 at idx37; idx39 col-only with (15,21,15)) confirmed; nu-distribution {0:145,2:1,6:1} confirmed both by aspect rule and by full 6-conjugate row-Hamiltonicity test, aspect mapping agrees. is7: 564 lines, 0/564 CSV mismatches; headline (2/2/2/1, atomic idx67, companions idx294/300/365) confirmed; nu {0:560,2:3,6:1} confirmed via conjugates. Atomic witness grid (mc idx37 compact 0123456130456220613453415620453620156420136250134) is Latin; all 63 stored perms are 7-cycles and each recomputes exactly from the grid under the paper's symbol-domain (row/col) and rows-domain (symbol) formulations; the identical row/col/sym lists are genuinely correct for this square (all three formulas coincide numerically, verified pair-by-pair). Z7=(21,21,21) and Z8=(16,16,16) confirmed; Z7 absent from both McKay lists as claimed. mc8 head-300: 300 Latin 8x8 lines, 0/300 mismatches, per-aspect maxima 16/16/16, zero with 28, as claimed. verify.py logic for counts and atomic recomputation is sound (its row/col/symbol formulas match the independent formulations; conjugate cross-check on mc39 gives [15,15,21,21,15,15], consistent with column-only status). Proof vs evidence distinguished: result is certified finite computation with replay, not a general theorem; no Allsop-Wanless nu=4>=11 bound is reproved, only consistency noted.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp/failed-search: (1) McKay database gives bare squares/counts only (verified live: 147 main-class / 564 isotopy at order 7, 283657 main-class at order 8) with no per-square Hamiltonian spectra, so tables are not transcription. (2) Allsop-Wanless arXiv:2211.13826 (Proc. LMS 2024) gives nu in {0,2,4,6} theory plus an infinite nu=4 structural family solving Falconer 1970, not a per-representative order-7 census. (3) Allsop-Wanless arXiv:2506.02455 enumerates P1Fs/row-Hamiltonian squares at order 11, different order, no order-7 cycle table. (4) Allsop arXiv:2302.12942 gives quadratic/anti-perfect constructions plus per-prime finiteness, not a census. (5) Gill-Wanless K16 enumeration notes no atomic order-15 from those P1Fs, different order/invariant. arXiv search 'atomic Latin squares' returns only the above two hits. No source gives per-rep Hamiltonian-pair counts, nu-distribution, or the idx37/idx67 atomic certificates at order 7. The facts are not mechanically implied by the general theorems; every cycle type must be regenerated from tables.

value.rationale: Headline is a rigorously established exact invariant of a natural, pre-motivated object: row/column/symbol-Hamiltonicity of the complete McKay order-7 representative lists, motivated before computation by the row-Hamiltonian = perfect 1-factorisation of K_n,n equivalence and the atomic (nu=6) / Falconer-variety program. The values (which reps are Hamiltonian/atomic, exact pair counts, nu-distribution, explicit 63-cycle atomic certificate) were not known and are not mechanically implied. A future researcher in 1-factorisation/atomic-square classification can reasonably need the precise per-rep fact and replayable certificate. This is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained number: definitions, nu interpretation, witness grid, and reuse path are given. The incomplete order-8 300-sample is honestly bounded (no claim on remaining 283357 classes) and does not erase the complete order-7 census; no general criterion, completed order-8 census, or downstream theorem is required for the admitted headline.
